title: Skip-Count Tables
big_idea: Tables are skip counts, and the last digits show a pattern
child_idea: A table is counting in jumps: the 5s are 5, 10, 15 and so on. 6 jumps of 5 is 6 × 5 = 30. The last digits make a pattern.

topics: Tables of 2, 5 and 10 as skip counts, multiplying within 40 (Primary 1, Multiplication and Division, p. 31)
Numbers that are in two tables (common multiples, Primary 4, p. 37)
moe.note: Strand label for the tutor only. The 2, 5 and 10 tables within 40 are Primary 1 content and fill Start here. BEYOND PRIMARY 1 ON PURPOSE: the 3 and 4 tables are Primary 2 content (p. 33) and numbers that are in two tables (common multiples) are Primary 4 content (p. 37), so Think harder (the 4s as doubled 2s, numbers in both the 2s and the 5s) and Go further (the 4s and 3s, three tables) go past the school Primary 1 syllabus. Tables of 6 to 9 are Primary 3 and are left out. Owner decision, 22 Oct 2026: strong content with scaffolding, said plainly to families. Say this on the parent page and in the opening of the guide; do not describe the lesson as MOE-aligned or syllabus-aligned. Reading order: 6 jumps of 5 is 6 × 5 (jumps first, then the size of the jump); either order is accepted in an answer. Contest tag (tutor only): numbers in two tables, shared multiples.

contest_moves: numbers that are in two tables (2s and 5s up to 40)
a table number can be tested by its last digit
objectives: Build the 5s, 2s and 10s by counting in jumps along a 100 square and say facts such as "6 fives is 30" and 6 × 5 = 30.
Say that a table is skip counting, tell 6 × 5 (6 jumps of 5) from 6 + 5, and write a missing number in a table row (products to 40).
Notice the last digits of each table: 5 or 0 for the 5s, 0 for the 10s and 0, 2, 4, 6 or 8 for the 2s.
Think harder: use the 2s to find the 4s (4 × 6 is double 2 × 6), find the numbers that are in both the 2s and the 5s, and test a number by its last digit.
Go further: the 4s and 3s tables to 40 and the numbers they share with the 5s.

remember: Count in 2s, 5s and 10s along a number square (Term 1)
Jumps of the same size along a number line (Term 1)
5 groups of 6 as repeated addition: 6 + 6 + 6 + 6 + 6 (Term 2 Lesson 5, taught again with a picture)
joining_cold.assumes: Only counting to 20 and adding small numbers. Nothing from an earlier lesson is needed: the warm-up counts in jumps on a number square, shows jumps on a number line and builds 5 groups of 6 with a picture and one addition at a time. The word table and the × sign are taught in Explore and the Mini-lesson.
holiday_topics_revisited: Skip counting in 2s, 5s and 10s (Count with the Frog)
joining_cold.note: Term 2 Lessons 5 to 8 build on one another (groups, tables, sharing, stories), so try not to miss this lesson. A child who misses it watches the recording and does workbook pages 1 and 2. A child who joins here without Term 2 Lesson 5 can follow, because the warm-up shows groups of as repeated addition and the Mini-lesson says the × sign again.

child: The printed workbook with the 100 square kit page (page 6): nothing to cut
2 or 3 coloured pencils (pencil crayons or crayons)
About 20 small things of one kind (counters, buttons, dry pasta, coins) to use as frogs or to count
A pencil, a rubber and spare paper
tutor: A paper copy of the 100 square and coloured pencils to show on camera if you wish
kit_pages: 100 square (page 6): the numbers 1 to 100. Nothing to cut. The counter frog starts just to the left of the 1, which is 0. Children colour on it lightly
materials.notes: No ruler is needed. Nothing needs to be bought: everything can be found at home. No matches, toothpicks or anything sharp. Small things never go near the mouth or ears. Pencil crayons are better than felt pens on the printed square.

timing.notes: Opening is 2 minutes (the routine and rules were taught earlier in the term; give the recording, muting and camera notice). Explore has 14 minutes on the 100 square: the 5s, then the 2s and 10s, then the last digits. The mini-lesson has 12 because it writes the facts down and separates 6 × 5 from 6 + 5. The last 5 minutes are the standing buffer; the optional Go further slide is used only if the lesson is on time.
skip_order: Start with: cut the Mini-lesson check slide to three facts
Then: shorten Explore round 3 to the 5s only
Then: take the extra minutes from the flex time

slides.title: Skip-Count Tables

blocks.head: TODAY WE WILL
items: Build tables by counting in jumps.

slides.note: Term 2 Lesson 6, 90 minutes. Objective: build the 5s, 2s and 10s tables by counting in jumps along a 100 square, say and write the facts (6 × 5 = 30), notice the last digits, and use the 2s to find the 4s (doubling, shown once in the Mini-lesson). Plain statement for families: the 2, 5 and 10 tables within 40 are Primary 1 work, but the 3 and 4 tables and numbers that are in two tables go past the school Primary 1 syllabus on purpose. Time plan: opening 0 to 2, warm-up 2 to 8, sneak-peek 8 to 12, explore 12 to 26, mini-lesson 26 to 38, brain break 38 to 42, workbook 42 to 70, talk 70 to 76, exit ticket 76 to 82, look-back 82 to 85, flex time and goodbye 85 to 90 (the buffer: do not start anything new). Think harder, Go further and the Investigation are for every child to choose. Greet by first name, then say the recording notice in one line (you and the screen only; a child may keep the camera off), then start the recording.
slides.subtitle: Counting in jumps: the 2s, 5s and 10s

mascot.say: Hi, I'm Mi. Let's notice, test and explain why!

slides.title: Warm-up: count in jumps

blocks.text: Touch the yellow numbers as we say them
Count in 2s: 2, 4, 6, 8 ...

items: 2s
5s

slides.note: The yellow numbers are the numbers we say when we count in twos. Count together to 18, touching each yellow number, then count in fives (5, 10, 15) and count in tens together (10, 20, 30, 40). Ask: after 18 in twos (20), after 35 in fives (40). No writing, no marks. A child who is unsure touches each number on the screen.

slides.title: Jumps on a number line

blocks.text: Every jump is the same size.

items: next jump
4 jumps of 5

slides.note: The frog jumps 5 each time and has made 2 jumps. Ask: where does the next jump land (15), where do 4 jumps of 5 land (20). Children answer aloud or with fingers. A child who is unsure counts the jumps on fingers while saying the numbers.

slides.title: 5 groups of 6

blocks.text: 6 + 6 + 6 + 6 + 6: add one group at a time.

slides.note: Five bags with 6 counters in each bag. We add one bag at a time: 6 + 6 = 12, then 12 + 6 = 18, and so on. Say 6 + 6 = 12 yourself, then ask: 12 + 6 (18). Children answer aloud. This is Term 2 Lesson 5 taught again: groups of is repeated addition, and a table is the same idea with the jump size fixed.

slides.title: Sneak-peek puzzles

blocks.text: Ideas we have not learnt yet. A guess is a great start. Nobody is marked.

cols.head: PUZZLE 1: anyone can try
items: Jenny puts 5 stickers on each page.
She fills 4 pages.
How many stickers is that altogether?
You may draw or count in 5s.

cols.head: PUZZLE 2: think
items: Ali counts in 2s: 2, 4, 6, 8 and so on up to 20.
Mei counts in 5s: 5, 10, 15, 20.
Which numbers do they both say?
Write them.

slides.note: Puzzle 1 (4 pages with 5 stickers; 20 stickers) is an access question: any child can draw or count in fives. Puzzle 2 is a thinking question on the lesson idea: numbers in two tables (10 and 20). Say: two sneak-peek puzzles, ideas we have not learnt yet; a guess is a great start and I do not know is welcome; nobody is marked. Children write on their own paper. Nobody holds paper to the camera. There is no private chat. Answers: 20; 10 and 20. Do not reveal puzzle 2 until Talk time. Do not write scores or keep a list.

slides.title: Explore: jumps of 5

items: Put a counter just left of the 1. That is 0.
Jump 5 at a time. Colour each number you land on.
Say it: 1 five is 5, 2 fives is 10, 3 fives is 15 ...
How many jumps to land on 30?

slides.note: Round 1, about 5 minutes. Children use the 100 square on the kit page (page 6) and a counter as a frog. Start on 0: the counter sits just to the left of the 1, off the square. Each jump of 5 lands on 5, 10, 15 ... up to 40; children colour each landing square lightly and say 1 five is 5, 2 fives is 10. Fingers count the jumps. Ask: how many jumps to land on 30 (6), on 25 (5), on 40 (8). Then say 6 fives is 30 and write 6 × 5 = 30 on the screen. The picture shows the numbers 1 to 40 with nothing coloured, so children find the landing numbers themselves.

slides.title: Jumps of 2 and of 10

blocks.text: Use a different colour for each table.

items: Jump 2 at a time: how many jumps to land on 12?
Jump 10 at a time: how many jumps to land on 40?

slides.note: Round 2, about 4 minutes. Children colour the 2s in a second colour and put a ring round the 10s. Ask: how many jumps of 2 to land on 12 (6; 6 twos is 12) and how many jumps of 10 to land on 40 (4; 4 tens is 40). Say each fact with the sign: 6 × 2 = 12, 4 × 10 = 40. A child who loses count uses fingers for the jumps. Do not name a child with a wrong answer.

slides.title: What do you notice?

blocks.text: Look at the last digits of the numbers you landed on.

items: The 5s end in ...
The 10s end in ...
The 2s end in ...

slides.note: Round 3, about 5 minutes. Ask: look at the last digit of each yellow number (the 5s). What do you notice? (5, 0, 5, 0). The 10s end in 0. The 2s end in 0, 2, 4, 6 or 8. Let children say the pattern themselves. Then ask: is 35 in the 5s? is 28? Children answer with a thumb up or down. The picture here shows the 5s as an example only. Accept any correct pattern a child finds, such as the 5s are every second number of the 10s.

slides.title: The 5s table
slides.note: A table is a list of jumps. The first number is how many jumps and the second is the size of each jump: 6 × 5 is 6 jumps of 5, which lands on 30. The table stops at 6 fives; 7 × 5 is asked aloud and the answer comes on the next slide. Link back to Term 2 Lesson 5: 6 groups of 5 and 6 jumps of 5 are the same.

slides.title: The 2s and the 10s

blocks.text: 4 × 2 = 8 and 3 × 10 = 30. The 2s go on 10, 12 and the 10s go on 40.

slides.note: The 2s are jumps of 2: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12. The 10s are jumps of 10: 10, 20, 30, 40. Say each fact. Ask: what is 4 × 2 (8), what is 3 × 10 (30); the answers come on the next slide. Children who know the facts say them aloud; others look at the card. Note the 10s are every second number of the 5s.

slides.title: Last digits

blocks.text: A last digit can tell you if a number is in a table.

slides.note: Last digits make a pattern. The 5s end in 5 or 0; the 10s always end in 0; the 2s end in 0, 2, 4, 6 or 8. Ask: is 35 in the 5s table (yes, it ends in 5)? Is 28 in the 5s table (no, it ends in 8)? Say that the last digit helps us test; a few tests do not prove a rule for every number, but the jumps show why.

slides.title: Add or jump?

blocks.text: The sign tells you what to do.

slides.note: A common mix-up is 6 + 5 and 6 × 5. 6 + 5 means 6 and 5 more: 11. 6 × 5 means 6 jumps of 5: 30. Ask: what is 4 + 3 and what is 4 × 3 (7 and 12)? Link to the pictures: 4 groups of 3 is 4 × 3.

slides.title: Double it

cols.text: The top 2 rows are in the box.

blocks.text: 2 × 6 = 12. All 4 rows are two lots of 12: 12 + 12 = 24, so 4 × 6 = 24.

slides.note: The 4s are the 2s doubled. The top 2 rows are 2 × 6 = 12. All 4 rows are two lots of the boxed rows, so 4 × 6 is 12 + 12 = 24. Ask for 2 × 6 first, then 4 × 6, and let children say the doubling themselves. The answer comes on the next slide. Workbook T1 uses the same idea with new numbers.

slides.title: Your turn

blocks.text: Write the fact and the total.

slides.note: Each child writes the three totals on their own paper, for example 7 × 2 = 14 (7 jumps of 2). Walk the cameras; do not ask children to hold papers up. Wait 10 seconds before helping. Answers: 14, 18, 20. Children may use the 100 square and a counter.

slides.title: Check: the facts
slides.note: Answers: 14, 18, 20. Read each answer aloud so a child watching the recording can mark their own work. Children tick their own. Never ask a child to show a wrong answer to the group.

slides.title: Whisper and say

blocks.text: I count from 1. On every fifth number, show 5 fingers and say it.
Then I count to 20. Clap softly on every second number.
Stand up. Sip some water.

slides.note: Four minutes. Stand up on camera. The tutor counts from 1 to 30 slowly. On every fifth number children show 5 fingers and say the number. Then 1 to 20: children clap softly on every second number. No equipment, no running, a little clear space. A child may stay seated. Do not give prizes or compare children.

slides.title: Workbook page 1: Start here

blocks.text: Questions 1 to 3. Take your time.

slides.note: Read questions 1 to 3 aloud. Children work on their own; the tutor walks the cameras and asks how do you know. Wait 10 seconds before helping. After question 3 any child may choose to carry on or try Think harder. Question 1: count in 5s and fill in three missing numbers. Question 2: a frog jumps on a number line. Question 3: 4 bundles of 10 straws.

slides.title: Check page 1
slides.note: Read each answer aloud. Children tick their own page. Never ask a child to show a wrong answer to the group. Answers: Q1 15, 25, 35; Q2 3 jumps, each jump 5, 3 × 5 = 15; Q3 40 straws.

slides.title: Workbook page 2: Start here

blocks.text: Questions 4 to 6. Take your time.

slides.note: Read questions 4 to 6 aloud. Question 4: 6 bikes with 2 wheels each. Question 5: a table of 5s facts with boxes. Question 6: true or false for four facts.

slides.title: Check page 2
slides.note: Read each answer aloud so a child watching the recording can mark their own work. Never ask a child to show a wrong answer to the group. Answers: Q4 12 and 12 wheels; Q5 10, 20, 30, 40; Q6 true, false, true, false.

slides.title: Choose your next page

rows: The 4s and numbers in two tables
Finish and check your own work

blocks.text: Everyone may choose. Not finished? Pages 3 to 5 are for home too.

slides.note: Invite the whole group at once, for example: when you have finished Start here, you can choose Think harder, Go further or the Investigation. Never announce who is on which page and never name a child. Pairs are not split unless both children agree. Model answers are in the tutor guide. About 5 minutes.

slides.title: Talk and explain

blocks.head: WEI SAYS
items: A number is in the 5s table if its last digit is 5 or 0.

blocks.text: Is Wei right? How could we test it?
I think ... because ...

slides.note: One minute of talk to the grown-up next to you, or to your screen. Children test Wei’s rule on the 100 square: 15, 40, 28, 33. Then volunteers first; a pass is always fine; never call a child by name to answer. Model answer: it works for the numbers we tested; the 5s alternate between ending in 5 and 0, so a number that ends in 5 or 0 is in the table, and one that ends in anything else is not. Repeat each child’s answer in your own words for the recording.

slides.title: Back to the sneak-peek

blocks.text: Yellow: 2s only. Green: 5s only. Border: both.
10 and 20 are in both. So are 30 and 40.

slides.note: Reveal puzzle 2 now. Say: many of you wrote a good reason. Do not read out anyone’s earlier answer. Ali’s twos and Mei’s fives meet at 10 and 20 (and later at 30 and 40). The numbers in both tables end in 0. Puzzle 1: 4 pages of 5 stickers is 20.

slides.title: Exit ticket

blocks.text: On your own. No looking back.

slides.note: Children answer on page 5. Read E1, E2 and E3 aloud (the questions are on the slide). Children tick their own ticket against the next slide. Nobody holds paper to the camera and there is no private chat.

slides.title: Check the exit ticket
slides.note: Read each answer aloud. Children tick their own ticket. Answers: 15 and 25; option 2, 4 × 10 = 40; 6 × 5 = 30 and 30 stickers.

slides.title: Look-back
slides.note: Three minutes. Children tick or write the look-back box on page 5. A pass is always allowed. It is never marked, never collected in front of the group and never read out. If a child ticks I am still stuck, a grown-up may photograph that page after class and send it to the business WhatsApp (the number is in the parent summary, never on a slide). You then help in the open session next lesson. Never a direct message to a child. The Next time I will try row is optional.

mascot.say: Take your time. You can pass.

slides.title: Well done, inquirers!

blocks.text: Show a grown-up one thing you found out today.

blocks.head: NEXT LESSON
items: Sharing and Grouping
Have ready: your Term 2 Lesson 7 workbook, about 20 counters or buttons, 5 plates or cups, pencil and paper.

slides.note: Say goodbye and thank the grown-ups. Minutes 85 to 90 are flex time: the buffer. If you ran late, finish any open item (the look-back). Do not start anything new. If the whole class is ahead, show the optional slides and use the Spare-time menu from the tutor guide.

slides.title: Go further: what if?

blocks.text: Ben says: every number in the 10s table is also in the 5s table.
Is Ben right?
Try 10, 20, 30 and 40 on your 100 square.

slides.note: Optional, only if you are on time. Answer: yes. Every jump of 10 is two jumps of 5, so a number in the 10s table is in the 5s table. Children try 10, 20, 30 and 40; say the answers aloud afterwards. Take two answers and move on.

slides.title: If we have time: pick one

rows: Every number in the 10s is in the 5s. Test it.
Pick a number to 40. Ask your grown-up: is it in the 5s table?
Show a toy how to find 6 × 5 by jumping

blocks.text: Optional. Everyone may join.

slides.note: Optional Spare-time menu, used only if the whole class is ahead. Pick one or two activities (3 to 5 minutes each); full tutor lines and answers are in the tutor guide. Never start new content and never name who is ahead. Slow down with how do you know rather than rushing on. These minutes come from the flex buffer and are not part of the 90-minute sum.

lines.text: Greet the whole group warmly, before the recording starts. Check that you can see each child, or ask the grown-up.
Hello, inquirers! Pencil ready, and your 100 square, coloured pencils and counters on the table. Cameras can be on or off, as you like.
This lesson is recorded so a friend who is away can catch up. The recording has me, the shared screen and any voice that is not muted. You may keep your microphone and camera off.
Start the recording now. Do not use children's first names on the recording.
@rec
Microphone off until I ask you to speak. To answer, say it with me on three, show fingers, or give a thumbs up. Nobody holds paper up to the camera.
Today we build tables by counting in jumps, and we look for patterns in the last digits. A table is just skip counting.

Say the recording statement and the microphone routine in the same words every lesson, for anyone who joined late. Say the notice before you start the recording, and do not use children's first names once it is running. The routine and the four inquirer rules were introduced earlier in the term: do not re-teach them.

Plain statement for families when it comes up: the 2, 5 and 10 tables within 40 are Primary 1 work, but the 3 and 4 tables and numbers that are in two tables are beyond Primary 1 on purpose, always with the 100 square and counters.

New here? Say in one minute: our three rule words (notice it, test it, explain why); a guess is fine and you can always pass; after Start here you may choose Think harder, Go further or the Investigation; nobody holds paper to the camera. The first recording of the term shows the full routine.
@rec
Counting in jumps. Touch the yellow numbers as we count in twos: two, four, six, eight. Count with me up to eighteen.
What comes after eighteen when we count in twos?
Now count in fives: five, ten, fifteen, twenty.
What comes after thirty-five when we count in fives?
And in tens: ten, twenty, thirty, forty. Count with me.
A frog jumps five each time. It has made two jumps. Every jump is the same size.
Where does the next jump land?
Where do four jumps of five land?
Five bags with six counters in each bag. We add one bag at a time: six and six make twelve.
Twelve plus six?

If a child is unsure about counting in jumps, touch each number on the screen and count slowly, one jump at a time on fingers. For the number line, count the jumps first, then read where the last one lands. For the bags, add one bag at a time and say the total each time.
Answers: 20, 40; 15, 20; 18. Children answer with a whisper, fingers or hands. Nobody writes. Do not say table yet. Joining cold: all you need is counting to 20 and adding small numbers.
@rec
Two sneak-peek puzzles: ideas we have not learnt yet. A guess is a great start, and I do not know is welcome. Nobody is marked.
Puzzle one. Jenny puts 5 stickers on each page. She fills 4 pages. How many stickers is that altogether? You may draw or count in 5s.
Children draw or count and write the number on their own paper.
Puzzle two. Ali counts in 2s: 2, 4, 6, 8 and so on up to 20. Mei counts in 5s: 5, 10, 15, 20. Which numbers do they both say? Write them.
Children write or draw their answer.
Keep your paper. Nobody shows it. We will check our own thinking later, at Talk time.
Puzzle 1 answer: 20 stickers. Puzzle 2 answer: 10 and 20. Look for good ideas to praise later (a child who wrote both lists). Do not write scores or keep a list.
@rec
Your hands are the teachers. Find the 100 square on your kit page. Put a counter just to the left of the one, off the square. That is zero. This is your frog.
Jump five at a time. Colour lightly each number you land on and say it: one five is five, two fives is ten, three fives is fifteen.
Children jump in fives and colour the landing numbers up to 40, saying 1 five is 5, 2 fives is 10 and so on.
How many jumps did it take to land on thirty?
How many jumps to land on twenty-five?
Six fives is thirty. We write it six times five is thirty.
Round two. Use a different colour. Jump two at a time and colour each number you land on.
Children jump in twos and colour the landing numbers up to 20 or more.
How many jumps of two to land on twelve?
Now jump ten at a time. Put a ring round each number you land on.
Children jump in tens and ring 10, 20, 30, 40.
How many jumps of ten to land on forty?
Round three. Look at the last digit of each number you landed on in fives.
What do you notice about the last digits of the fives? What about the tens, and the twos?
The fives end in five or zero. The tens always end in zero. The twos end in zero, two, four, six or eight.
Is thirty-five in the 5s? Is twenty-eight? Thumb up or thumb down.

A child who loses their place: put the counter back on the last number they know and count the jumps again. A child who colours every number: say, only the numbers we land on. A child who starts on 1 instead of 0: the first jump from 0 lands on 5.

Main room only; children say their answers aloud and show fingers; you cannot see colouring on small tiles. Answers: 6, 5, 8 jumps of 5 (30, 25, 40); 6 jumps of 2 to 12; 4 jumps of 10 to 40; 35 is in the 5s and 28 is not. Colour lightly with pencil crayon. Accept any correct pattern a child finds. Do not call it a table yet beyond saying the 5s are a table.
@rec
A table is a list of jumps. Look at the fives. One jump of five is five. Two jumps of five is ten. Six fives is thirty. We write it six times five is thirty.
What is seven times five? How do you know?
The twos: two, four, six. The tens: ten, twenty. Say each fact with me.
What is four times two? What is three times ten?
The last digits make a pattern. The fives end in five or zero. The tens end in zero. The twos end in zero, two, four, six or eight.
Is thirty-five in the 5s table? Is twenty-eight? How do you know?
Take care with the sign. Six plus five means six and five more. Six times five means six jumps of five.
What is four plus three? What is four times three?
Doubling helps with the fours. Look at the dots. The top 2 rows are in the box: two rows of six.
What is two times six? All four rows are two lots of the boxed rows. What is four times six?
Your turn. Write the fact and the total. Seven times two. Nine times two. Two times ten.
Children write the three totals on their own paper.
Fourteen. Eighteen. Twenty. Tick your own.

Key words to use every time: table, jump, times, in a table, last digit. Say 6 jumps of 5 for 6 × 5. The 2, 5 and 10 tables within 40 are Primary 1 work; the 3 and 4 tables are beyond it on purpose and come in Think harder and Go further. Do not teach the tables by heart: the counting is the method. Accept 5 × 6 as a correct way to write the same total.
If a child writes 6 + 5 for 6 times 5, ask them to jump: start on 0 and jump 5 six times. If a child says a number is in a table without checking, ask: how can we test it?
@rec
Stand up and get a sip of water. I count from one. On every fifth number, show five fingers and say the number.
Count 1 to 30 slowly. Children show 5 fingers and say every fifth number. Then count 1 to 20 and children clap softly on every second number. Children may stay seated.
@rec

Page 1, Start here. Question 1: count in 5s and fill in the missing numbers. Question 2: a frog jumps on a number line. Fill in the blanks. Question 3: Ravi has 4 bundles of 10 straws. How many straws does Ravi have in all?
Page 1, questions 1 to 3. Tutor walks the cameras, asks how do you know. Wait 10 seconds before helping.
Question 1: 15, 25, 35. Question 2: 3 jumps, each jump 5, and 3 times 5 is 15. Question 3: 10, 20, 30, 40: 40 straws. Tick your own page.
After question 3 you may choose: carry on, or try Think harder. Everyone may choose, at any time.

start.text: Count in 5s. Fill in the missing numbers.
start.hint: Add 5 each time. Say the numbers: 5, 10, 15 ...
start.solution: Counting in 5s: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35, 40. The missing numbers are 15, 25 and 35.

start.text: A frog jumps along the number line. Fill in the blanks.
start.answer: 3 jumps; each jump is 5; 3 × 5 = 15 (5 × 3 = 15 is also right)
start.hint: Count the jumps. Then read the number on one jump.
start.solution: The frog makes 3 jumps and each jump is 5. 5 + 5 + 5 = 15, so 3 jumps of 5 is 3 × 5 = 15.
mistakes: Counting the numbers on the line instead of the jumps.

start.text: Ravi has 4 bundles of 10 straws. How many straws does Ravi have in all?
start.solution: 4 bundles of 10: 10 + 10 + 10 + 10 = 40. So 4 × 10 = 40 and Ravi has 40 straws.

start.text: Each bike has 2 wheels. How many wheels do 6 bikes have?
start.hint: Count in 2s: 2, 4, 6 ... Use your fingers for the bikes.

mistakes: Writing the number of jumps in the Total box.

start.text: Read each statement. Decide if it is True or False.
start.hint: Count the jumps for each fact, or use your 100 square.
start.solution: 5 × 4 = 20 is true. 3 × 10 is 30, not 40: false. 6 × 2 = 12 is true. 8 × 5 is 40, not 35: false.
mistakes: Marking 8 × 5 = 35 as true because it ends in 5.

think.text: Look at the dots. The top 2 rows are in the box. Fill in the blanks.
think.hint: The 4 rows are two lots of the 2 boxed rows.
think.solution: 2 rows of 5 dots is 2 × 5 = 10. All 4 rows are two lots of 10 dots: 10 + 10 = 20, so 4 × 5 = 20.

think.text: Colour the 2s. Ring the 5s. Then fill in the blanks.

parts.text: The numbers in both tables are [2], [2], [2] and [2].

think.hint: Look for the numbers that are coloured and ringed.
think.solution: The 2s are 2, 4, 6 ... 40. The 5s are 5, 10, 15 ... 40. The numbers in both are 10, 20, 30 and 40.

think.text: Is each number in the 5s table? Circle Yes or No.
think.hint: Look at the last digit. Count in 5s if you are not sure.
think.solution: 50 ends in 0: yes. 27 ends in 7: no. 65 ends in 5: yes.
mistakes: Saying 27 is in the table because it is close to 25.
Saying 65 is not in the table because it is a big number.

go.text: Here are the 4s up to 40. Ring each number that is also in the 5s table. Then fill in the blanks.

parts.text: Numbers in the 4s and the 5s: [2] and [2].

go.hint: Check each number in the 4s: does it end in 5 or 0?
go.solution: The 4s are 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 28, 32, 36, 40. The ones that end in 5 or 0 are 20 and 40.
mistakes: Ringing 16 or 24 (they do not end in 0 or 5).

go.text: Count in 3s up to 30. Fill in the missing numbers. Then find the numbers in both the 3s and the 5s.

parts.text: In both the 3s and the 5s: [2] and [2].

go.solution: The 3s are 3, 6, 9, 12, 15, 18, 21, 24, 27, 30. The 5s up to 30 are 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30. The numbers in both are 15 and 30.
mistakes: Writing 10 for a number in both tables.

go.text: Ali jumps 5 each time. Mei jumps 4 each time. They both want to reach 40.

parts.text: Mei needs [] more jumps than Ali.

go.hint: How many jumps of 5 land on 40? How many jumps of 4?
go.solution: 8 jumps of 5 make 40 (8 × 5 = 40). 10 jumps of 4 make 40 (10 × 4 = 40). 10 - 8 = 2 more jumps.
mistakes: Guessing the number of jumps of 4 without counting in 4s.
Forgetting to subtract at the end.

investigation.title: Last digits
investigation.first: Write the last digit of each number in the 5s up to 40: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35, 40.
investigation.text: Which of 10, 15, 20 and 25 are in both the 2s and the 5s? Write the last digit of each one you find. Write what you notice.
investigation.answer: 10 and 20 are in both tables (15 and 25 are only in the 5s). Both end in 0. The 5s end in 5 or 0 and the 2s end in 0, 2, 4, 6 or 8: the only digit in both lists is 0.
investigation.look_for: A child who tests several numbers, writes the last digits of both tables and sees that only 0 is in both lists. Credit any clear reason. Do not mark a child down for stopping at a few tests.
mistakes: Testing 15 and 25 and thinking they are in the 2s.

talk.question: Wei says: a number is in the 5s table if its last digit is 5 or 0. Is Wei right? How could we test it?
talk.answer: It works for 15 and 40, which end in 5 and 0. The 5s end in 5 and 0 one after the other, so a number ending in anything else, like 28 or 33, is not in the table. We tested a few numbers, and the jumps show why.
talk.look_for: A child who tests more numbers, uses the 100 square or says the last digits alternate. Not just "yes" or "no".

exit.text: Count in 5s. Fill in the missing numbers.
Which sentence is true? Write its number in the bracket.
Ben puts 5 stickers on each of 6 pages. How many stickers does Ben have in all?
exit.solution: 6 pages with 5 stickers on each page: 6 jumps of 5 land on 30.

home_practice.text: Count in 2s. Fill in the blanks. 2, 4, 6, [], 10, [2]
Count in 5s. Fill in the blanks. 5, [2], 15, [2], 25, [2]
A bundle has 10 straws. How many straws are in 3 bundles? 3 × 10 = [2]
Which numbers up to 20 are in both the 2s and the 5s? Write them. [2] and [2]
home_practice.solution: The 5s are 5, 10, 15, 20. The 2s include 10 and 20 but not 5 or 15.

items.q: A frog jumps 5 each time. Where does it land after 3 jumps?

slips.say: 8 is 3 + 5. The frog jumps 5 three times.

tpl.q: A frog jumps {b} each time. Where does it land after {a} jumps?

items.q: Count in 5s up to 30. Type the numbers with a comma between.

tpl.q: Count in {k}s up to {lim}. Type the numbers with a comma between.

items.hint: Look at the last digit, or count in 5s.

tpl.hint: Look at the last digit, or count in 5s.
steps: Look at the last digit of {n}.

slips.say: 4 + 5 is 4 and 5 more. 4 × 5 is 4 jumps of 5.

items.q: How many jumps of 5 does it take to land on 15?

slips.say: 5 is the size of the jump. How many jumps?

tpl.q: How many jumps of {k} does it take to land on {t}?
tpl.hint: Count the jumps: {k}, then {k} more, and so on.

items.q: Which numbers are in both the 2s and the 5s? Count to 40. Type the numbers with a comma between.
items.hint: Write the 5s, then keep the ones in the 2s.

tpl.q: Which numbers are in both the 2s and the 5s? Count to {lim}. Type the numbers with a comma between.
tpl.hint: Write the 5s, then keep the ones in the 2s.

items.q: Which number is in both the 2s and the 5s?

slips.say: 15 is in the 5s but not in the 2s: it is odd.

items.q: Mei counts in 5s. What is the 4th number she says?

tpl.q: Mei counts in 5s. What is the {j|ord} number she says?

items.q: Ali jumps 5 each time and Mei jumps 4 each time. They both reach 40. How many more jumps does Mei make than Ali?
items.hint: Count the jumps each child needs.

slips.say: 8 is Ali’s jumps. How many more does Mei need?

tpl.q: Ali jumps {a} each time and Mei jumps {b} each time. They both reach 40. How many more jumps does Mei make than Ali?
tpl.hint: Count the jumps each child needs.

items.q: Which numbers up to 40 are in the 4s and also in the 5s? Type the numbers with a comma between.
items.hint: Write the 4s: 4, 8, 12 ... Which ones end in 5 or 0?

items.q: Pick a number up to 40. Ask a grown-up: is it in the 5s table? Check by counting in jumps. Many answers are right.
items.hint: Look at the last digit first.
steps: Say what you think and why.

spare_time.note: Optional time, never added to the 90-minute sum. It comes from the 5-minute flex buffer, from slack in the parts, or from the optional Go further slide.
rules: Whole class ahead: use the Spare-time menu in the Flex time and the optional Go further slide. Pick one or two activities; do not start new content.
A few children ahead: they may choose Go further or the Investigation, which are open to everyone. Never label or name a child, and never announce who is ahead.
Never teach anything the next lesson needs. If the class is ahead, slow down: ask ‘How do you know?’ and let children explain, rather than rushing on.

menu.title: Is it always true?
menu.tutor: Ben says: every number in the 10s table is also in the 5s table. Test 10, 20, 30 and 40. Can you find a number in the 10s that is not in the 5s?
menu.rec: Recording: pause. Test 10, 20, 30 and 40 in the 5s table. Can you find a number in the 10s that is not in the 5s?
menu.answer: All four are in the 5s: 2, 4, 6 and 8 jumps of 5. No number breaks it: each jump of 10 is two jumps of 5.

menu.title: Make a puzzle for your grown-up
menu.tutor: Pick a number up to 40. Ask your grown-up: is it in the 5s table? Then check by counting in jumps of 5.
menu.rec: Recording: pause. Pick a number to 40. Ask a grown-up if it is in the 5s table, then check by counting.
menu.answer: No single answer. Check with the last digit (5 or 0 means yes) and by counting in 5s.

menu.title: Teach it back
menu.tutor: Pretend your grown-up or a toy has never met a table. Show them how to find 6 × 5 by jumping in 5s on the 100 square.
menu.rec: Recording: pause. Show a grown-up how to find 6 × 5 by jumping in 5s on the 100 square.

parent.summary: We built the 5s, 2s and 10s tables by counting in jumps along a 100 square and wrote the facts, such as 6 × 5 = 30. We looked at the last digits: the 5s end in 5 or 0, the 10s end in 0. The 2, 5 and 10 tables within 40 are Primary 1 work. The 4s (the 2s doubled), the 3s and numbers that are in two tables go past the school Primary 1 syllabus on purpose, always with the 100 square and counters.
words: table: counting in jumps of the same size
last digit: the ones digit of a number
in both tables: a number we say in two different counts
try_home: Jumps: count in 5s to 40 on the 100 square page. Colour each landing number. How many jumps to 30?
Detective: is 35 in the 5s table? Is 28? Ask your child how they know (look at the last digit).
Double it: if 2 × 6 = 12, what is 4 × 6? Show it with dots or 24 buttons in rows.
ask: How many jumps? What size is each jump?
How do you know it is in the table?
parent.when_stuck: Please count in jumps rather than chanting the table by heart. Either order is fine for your child’s own sentence: 6 × 5 and 5 × 6 both make 30. Let your child count the jumps on fingers or move a counter along the 100 square, and wait 10 seconds before helping. If the look-back page says ‘I am still stuck’, photograph it and send it to our business WhatsApp (+65 9880 5962). Photos are kept 90 days after the program ends.
parent.next: Term 2 Lesson 7: Sharing and Grouping. Online practice: your tutor shares the link. A missing workbook page: your tutor sends a PDF to print at 100%. The recording has the tutor, the shared screen and any voice that is not muted; your child may mute and keep the camera off. To have your child muted, tell us when you register. The link is private to your group's families: please do not share it.
parent.quote: A table is counting in jumps, and the last digits show a pattern.
parent.report_line: Your child is learning that a times table is counting in jumps and that the last digits show patterns. This week: the 2s, 5s and 10s, with the 4s and 3s as extras.
parent.term_line: This term: equal groups so far; now tables by counting in jumps; next, sharing, grouping and stories.
next_materials: Your Term 2 Lesson 7 workbook (it has a groups mat; nothing to cut)
5 plates or cups (paper plates are fine)

safeguarding: Counters and small things stay on the table: nothing goes in the mouth or ears. No matches, toothpicks or anything sharp. Keep small things away from younger brothers and sisters. Colour lightly with pencil crayons.
This lesson uses the main room only: no breakout rooms, so the tutor sees every camera. A parent sits nearby but does not give answers.

Nobody holds paper or a board up to the camera: a gallery view shows everyone. Children tick their own work against the answer slide, answer together on a count of three, or show fingers or a thumb for a choice. There is no private chat.

Never read out a child’s name with a right or wrong answer. The recording has the tutor, the shared screen and any voice that is not muted. Children may mute and keep their cameras off. A child’s page is never shown.
Movement break: children need a little clear space, soft shoes or socks on a safe floor, no stairs and no running. Counting aloud is quiet; a child may stay seated.

A child who is still stuck ticks ‘I am still stuck’ on the look-back page. A grown-up may photograph that page after class and send it to the business WhatsApp only; photos are kept for 90 days after the program ends. The tutor then helps in the open session next lesson. No private messages to children, and no personal phones.
The look-back is never collected in front of the group or read out. A pass is always allowed.
tutor_prep: Solve every workbook question yourself first. Check the lists for T2 (10, 20, 30, 40), G1 (20, 40) and G2 (15, 30) so you can answer a child who finds another number in two tables.

Tell parents a week before: use the workbook pages from the printed term book (send a PDF only if a page is missing, to print at 100%); the 100 square kit page needs no cutting, and find coloured pencils and about 20 small things. Small things stay away from mouths and younger children. Check each family has the next workbook in their term book (it has the groups mat); send a PDF only if a page is missing.
Have the slides open and check the 100 square is visible on screen share. Have your own 100 square and a counter to show on camera if you wish.

Check the recording captures the tutor and the shared screen. Children's video is excluded; any voice that is not muted is recorded. Greet the whole group warmly, say the recording notice, then start the recording, and do not use children's first names while it runs.

Be plain with families: the 2, 5 and 10 tables within 40 are Primary 1 work, but the 3 and 4 tables and numbers that are in two tables are beyond the school Primary 1 syllabus on purpose. Do not call the lesson MOE-aligned. Do not teach tables by heart; the jumps are the method. Term 2 Lessons 5 to 8 build on one another.

workbook.hint_p1: Use your 100 square and a counter. In 3 × 5, the first number is how many jumps and the second is the size of each jump.
workbook.hint_p2: Use your 100 square to count the jumps.

workbook.hint_p4: Choose any question. You do not have to finish them all.
